items.topic: Radial tunnel and deep radial nerve/PIN compression anatomy
items.destination_intent: Hand 2026 teaching note when OITE logging is requested
items.teaching_point_placement: Beside the distinction between the arcade of Frohse at the proximal supinator entrance and the distal supinator exit
items.caption_intent: Exact uploaded operative figure labeled posterior interosseous nerve and distal edge of supinator. This illustrates a potential distal compression site, distinct from the proximal arcade of Frohse, which is the keyed most common site in Q94.

items.topic: Radial tunnel and deep radial nerve/PIN compression anatomy
items.destination_intent: Hand 2026 teaching note when OITE logging is requested
items.teaching_point_placement: Immediately beside the operative distal supinator figure and the radial nerve branching explanation
items.caption_intent: Exact user-uploaded labeled radial tunnel diagram. The radial nerve splits into superficial and deep branches; the deep branch enters supinator at the arcade of Frohse, travels through supinator and exits distally as the PIN. The ECRB fibrous edge and distal supinator edge are other potential compression sites.

items.topic: Ligament of Struthers versus arcade of Struthers and arcade of Frohse
items.destination_intent: Hand 2026 teaching note when OITE logging is requested
items.teaching_point_placement: Within Q94 named nerve compression sites, next to the median nerve versus ulnar nerve distinction for the two Struthers structures
items.caption_intent: Exact user-uploaded diagram of the median nerve passing beneath the ligament of Struthers, which connects a supracondylar process to the medial epicondyle in the classic configuration. Distally, the median nerve passes between the humeral and ulnar heads of pronator teres. This ligament is distinct from the arcade of Struthers on the ulnar nerve course.
